---
title: "Coordinates and volumes"
---

The IBL atlas describes a position in the brain in one of two ways: as a coordinate in metres
relative to bregma, or as an index into an image volume. Coordinates are in the IBL frame; for
how it relates to the Allen CCF, see [Atlas spaces and transforms](atlas-spaces.qmd). This page
explains the axes, units and origin of coordinates and indices, and how the two differ.

## The three axes

| Axis | Position in a coordinate | Axis in a volume | Positive | Negative |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **ML** (`x`) | 1st | 2nd | right | left |
| **AP** (`y`) | 2nd | 1st | anterior to bregma | posterior to bregma |
| **DV** (`z`) | 3rd | 3rd | dorsal to bregma | ventral to bregma |

Deeper is more negative on the DV axis. A probe driven into the brain moves towards more
negative `z`, so a point 4 mm below bregma has a `z` of `-0.004`.

## Coordinates are in metres

Coordinates are in metres, relative to bregma, in the order (ML, AP, DV). A point 2 mm anterior
of bregma has an AP coordinate of `0.002`.

## Volumes are ordered (AP, ML, DV)

The image volumes order their axes (AP, ML, DV): the first two are swapped relative to a
coordinate. Under C-ordering, this layout makes coronal slices the fastest to read. The origin
of a volume is the top-left corner of the image.

So `volume[i, j, k]` is AP index `i`, ML index `j` and DV index `k`, while a coordinate
`(x, y, z)` is ML, AP, DV.

The gene-expression volumes use a different order, (ML, DV, AP) — see
[External data in the common space](external-data-in-the-common-space.qmd).

## Bregma is the origin

Bregma is at voxel `(5739, 5400, 332)` µm in the Allen volume, in (ML, AP, DV) order. Coordinates
are measured from this point, so bregma itself is `(0, 0, 0)`.

## Indices and coordinates

An index and a coordinate describe a position in different ways:

- an **index** is a position in the array: an integer, which depends on the volume's
  resolution, counted from the corner of the volume;
- a **coordinate** is a position in the brain: a float, in metres, measured from bregma.

A coordinate is the same at every resolution. Its index is not: the same point has different
indices in a 10 µm volume and in a 25 µm volume.

## Atlases with a rotation

`BrainCoordinates` holds one (4, 4) affine `matrix` that maps volume indices to coordinates. For
the Allen, Needles and MRI Toronto atlases it is diagonal, an origin and a voxel size per axis, so
each axis converts on its own (`x2i`, `i2x`, `xscale`, `dx`...). `Qiu2018Atlas` adds a rotation
about the ML axis, which mixes AP and DV: `xyz2i` and `i2xyz` still convert points, but the
per-axis methods raise a `ValueError` for an axis that the rotation touches, and so do the slice
and surface plots and the `Insertion` methods that use the brain surface. The ML axis is untouched
by a pitch, so it keeps working. See
[The Qiu 2018 atlas and its 5° pitch](atlas-spaces.qmd#the-qiu-2018-atlas-and-its-5-pitch).
